mainTopic: When the loaves of a תודה become holy: location, baking, extra loaves, and problems with the slaughter
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about the forty loaves that come with a תודה. The loaves do not become holy if they are outside the wall or not yet crusted when the animal is slaughtered. רבי יוחנן says 'the wall' means the wall of בית פאגי. ריש לקיש says it means the wall of the עזרה, because the word 'על' requires the loaves to be nearby. The גמרא explains why they repeat the same argument they had about slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ, and it brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. Next, a ברייתא learns from one פסוק three rules: the loaves need a crust, they become holy at the slaughter, and a slaughter שלא לשמה does not make them holy. רבא adds that half-baked bread, like מצה נא, counts for the תודה loaves. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן then argue about a תודה slaughtered with eighty loaves, and רבי זירא, אביי and רב פפא each explain that argument differently. Finally, a new משנה lists which problems still let the loaves become holy. The גמרא says it follows רבי מאיר: a problem before the slaughter means the bread does not become holy, and a problem after it means the bread does.

steps.title: Loaves outside the wall do not become holy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the תודה is slaughtered inside but its loaves are outside the wall, the loaves do not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters the תודה in its proper place inside, but its bread is outside the wall, the bread does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first rule. The loaves only become holy through the שחיטה if they are in the right place when it happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה comes with forty loaves, and normally the שחיטה is what makes them holy. The משנה says this does not work when the loaves are 'outside the wall.' It does not tell us which wall it means, and the גמרא will ask about that soon.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering, which comes with forty loaves
Inside, in the proper place for שחיטה

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slaughters the thanks offering inside
and its bread is outside the wall,
the bread did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַתּוֹדָה לִפְנִים וְלַחְמָהּ חוּץ לַחוֹמָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves of a תודה that are outside the wall at the time of שחיטה are not made holy.

steps.title: Loaves not yet crusted do not become holy
steps.stepSummary: If the תודה is slaughtered before the loaves have formed a crust in the oven, the loaves do not become holy, even if only one loaf is unfinished.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it before the surface of the loaves formed a crust in the oven, the bread does not become holy. This is true even if all of them crusted except for one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case where the loaves don't become holy: they weren't baked enough yet when the animal was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves have to be real, finished bread at the time of שחיטה, meaning they have at least formed a crust. The משנה adds that even one unfinished loaf is enough to stop the whole set from becoming holy.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that most loaves being finished is good enough. The משנה says that if even one loaf has not crusted, the bread does not become holy.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחָטָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרְמוּ פָּנֶיהָ בַּתַּנּוּר,
phrases.english: If he slaughtered it before its surface formed a crust in the oven,
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the bread of the תודה, talking about all the loaves as if they were one.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ קָרְמוּ כּוּלָּן חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: and even if all of them formed a crust except for one of them,
the bread did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרְמוּ פָּנֶיהָ בַּתַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the משנה where the loaves are not made holy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loaves that have not all formed a crust at the time of שחיטה are not made holy.

steps.title: Which wall does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'outside the wall' in the משנה refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'outside the wall' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a clarifying question about the first rule of the משנה. This sets up the מחלוקת that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are several walls: the wall of the עזרה, and the wall around the area where holy foods may be eaten. The משנה's wording could fit more than one of them, so the גמרא needs to know which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is meant by 'outside the wall'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first case of the משנה to define its term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which wall the משנה means by 'outside the wall.'

steps.title: Two answers: the wall of בית פאגי or the wall of the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה means the wall of בית פאגי. ריש לקיש says it means the wall of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it means outside the wall of בית פאגי. ריש לקיש says it means outside the wall of the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, loaves that are just outside the עזרה are already 'outside the wall' and do not become holy. According to רבי יוחנן, the loaves only fail to become holy if they are much further away, outside בית פאגי.

keyTerms.meaning: Name of an outer wall in ירושלים, the edge of the area where the loaves may be eaten
The wall of the Temple courtyard

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: outside the wall of Beit Pagei,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת הָעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish says: outside the wall of the Temple courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת הָעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן says it is the wall of בית פאגי. ריש לקיש says it is the wall of the עזרה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reason: the loaves must be nearby
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the wall of the עזרה is meant because the word 'על' requires the loaves to be close to the תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says it means outside the wall of the עזרה, because we require 'על', meaning nearby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש holds his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the תודה is brought 'על', together with the loaves. ריש לקיש reads that word as 'right next to.' Loaves outside the עזרה are not next to the animal being slaughtered, so they do not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: With / upon, a word from the פסוק about the תודה

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת הָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: outside the wall of the Temple courtyard,
since we require 'with,' meaning nearby.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12. The word 'על' there links the loaves to the תודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for ריש לקיש's answer in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves must be close to the תודה at the שחיטה, so loaves outside the עזרה do not become holy.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: nearness is not required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says only loaves outside בית פאגי fail to become holy. Loaves just outside the עזרה do become holy, because he does not require them to be nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it means outside the wall of בית פאגי. But loaves that are only outside the עזרה do become holy, because we do not require 'על' to mean nearby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's view and how it differs from ריש לקיש's view in the case of loaves that are just outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not read 'על' as 'right next to.' So the loaves do not have to be in the עזרה. They only fail to become holy if they are outside בית פאגי, where they could not be eaten at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is holy (the bread does become holy)

steps.whatToRemember: Loaves outside the עזרה but inside בית פאגי: according to רבי יוחנן they become holy. According to ריש לקיש they do not, because he requires the loaves to be nearby ('על' בסמוך).
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole מחלוקת depends on how to read one word in the פסוק, 'על'. It also defines how close the loaves must be for the שחיטה to make them holy.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: outside the wall of Beit Pagei,
but if it is outside the courtyard, it is holy,
phrases.notes: He means loaves that are past the עזרה wall but still inside בית פאגי.

phrases.english: and we do not require 'with' to mean nearby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל חוּץ לָעֲזָרָה – קָדוֹשׁ, וְלָא בָּעֵינַן ״עַל״ בְּסָמוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reasoning, which is the opposite of ריש לקיש's reading in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loaves outside the עזרה but inside בית פאגי do become holy, because the loaves do not need to be nearby.

steps.title: Didn't they already argue about this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש need to argue about the תודה loaves, since they already argued about the same idea somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't they already disagree about this one time before?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the dispute from Steps 4-6, asking why we need it at all. It is setting up the next step, where it will show the other place they argued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute was really about the word 'על' and how close the loaves must be to the תודה. If the same two אמוראים already argued about 'על' in another case, this second argument looks like a repeat.

phrases.english: But didn't they already disagree about this one time?
phrases.notes: "They" are רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and "this" is how close something must be to count as 'על'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the dispute laid out in Steps 4-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about the תודה loaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two אמוראים should not need to repeat the same disagreement in a second case. If they already argued about the meaning of 'על', the second dispute seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The earlier dispute about slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about slaughtering the פסח 'על' חמץ. On that משנה, ריש לקיש requires the חמץ to be with the person in the עזרה, and רבי יוחנן does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who slaughters the פסח while owning חמץ breaks a לא תעשה. רבי יהודה says: the same is true of the תמיד. ריש לקיש said: He is only liable if the חמץ belongs to the one slaughtering, the one sprinkling the blood, or one of the group members, and it is with him in the עזרה. רבי יוחנן said: He is liable even if it is not with him in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves its challenge. There is a case where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already argued about whether 'על' means 'nearby'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids slaughtering the פסח 'על חמץ'. ריש לקיש reads 'על' as needing the חמץ to be close, inside the עזרה, just as he said about the loaves in Step 5. רבי יוחנן says nearness is not needed, just as he said in Step 6. So it looks like the very same argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering, here the afternoon one on ערב פסח
The כהן who sprinkles the blood
The group registered to eat a single קרבן פסח

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הֶחָמֵץ
phrases.english: As we learned: One who slaughters the פסח while owning חמץ
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פסחים 63a, based on שמות 34:25. Notice the same word 'על' again.

phrases.english: transgresses a negative commandment.
רבי יהודה says: Even the daily offering.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב
phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said: He is never liable

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אוֹ לַשּׁוֹחֵט, אוֹ לַזּוֹרֵק,
phrases.english: unless the חמץ belongs to the slaughterer, or to the one who sprinkles the blood,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְאֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה – עִמּוֹ בָּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: or to one of the group members, and it is with him in the עזרה.
And רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ בַּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: Even if it is not with him in the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up the challenge in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already argued about whether 'על' requires nearness
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פסחים about slaughtering the פסח 'על החמץ', and the dispute of the two אמוראים on it

steps.title: Both disputes are needed: רבי יוחנן might have agreed about the loaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers צריכא. If we only had the פסח case, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש about the loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If it were said only about that case of the פסח, we would say that only there רבי יוחנן holds his view, because wherever the חמץ is, the owner is standing in a prohibition. But about the loaves becoming holy, you might say he agrees with ריש לקיש: if they are inside, they become holy, and if they are outside, they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It explains that we need the dispute about the loaves, because from the פסח case alone we could not know רבי יוחנן's view on the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסח case, the owner is breaking the איסור of owning חמץ no matter where it is, so nearness might not matter there. Making loaves holy has no such reason. So רבי יוחנן might have required the loaves to be inside the עזרה. The loaves dispute teaches that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; both statements are needed
He is standing in a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's 'outside' here is just outside the עזרה. Even he agrees that loaves outside the wall of בית פאגי do not become holy (Step 6).

phrases.english: It is necessary, for if it were stated only about that case,
only in that case would רבי יוחנן say his view,
since wherever it is, he stands in a prohibition,
phrases.notes: Wherever the חמץ is, the owner is already breaking the rule against owning חמץ, so distance doesn't help him.

phrases.english: but regarding making the loaves holy,
I might say he agrees with ריש לקיש
that if they are inside, they become holy,
and if outside, they do not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 7-8 by showing the פסח dispute alone would not teach רבי יוחנן's view on the loaves.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reason, so both disputes are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the פסח case alone, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees that the loaves must be inside the עזרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaves dispute teaches that רבי יוחנן does not require nearness even for making the loaves holy.

steps.title: Both disputes are needed: ריש לקיש might have agreed about the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. If we only had the loaves case, we might think ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן about the פסח. So both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were said only about this case of the loaves, we would say that only here ריש לקיש holds his view. But about that case of the פסח, you might say he agrees with רבי יוחנן. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the other side. The פסח dispute is also needed, because from the loaves case alone we would not know ריש לקיש's view on the פסח. Then it concludes that both disputes are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason from Step 9 cuts the other way for ריש לקיש. In the פסח case the owner is breaking an איסור wherever the חמץ is, so ריש לקיש might have agreed there that nearness is not needed. The פסח dispute teaches that even there he requires the חמץ to be in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: In this case / in that case
I might say, you might think

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about 'על' both for the פסח with חמץ and for the תודה loaves. Each case has its own reason that could have changed one of their minds, so the גמרא needs both disputes (צריכא).

phrases.english: And if it were stated only about this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is the תודה loaves; "that case" in the next lines is the פסח with חמץ.

phrases.english: only in this case would ריש לקיש say his view,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: but in that case, I might say he agrees with רבי יוחנן,
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא from Step 9 by giving the other side and closing with צריכא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: the second half of the answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the loaves case alone, we might think ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן about the פסח with חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both disputes are necessary. Each one teaches something the other could not.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says loaves outside the wall of בית פאגי do not become holy, which matches רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits רבי יוחנן: if someone slaughters the תודה inside the עזרה while its loaves are outside the wall of בית פאגי, the loaves do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן in his argument with ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names the wall of בית פאגי as the line. So loaves inside בית פאגי, even if they are outside the עזרה, do become holy. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's view, against ריש לקיש, who requires the loaves to be in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him; supporting his view
The wall of בית פאגי, the outer area of ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: only loaves outside בית פאגי fail to become holy.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with Rabbi Yochanan:
One who slaughters the thanks offering inside,
phrases.notes: "Inside" means inside the עזרה, the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: and its loaves are outside the wall of Beit Pagei –
the loaves did not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש discussion with support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that only loaves outside בית פאגי fail to become holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that names the wall of בית פאגי as the line

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about loaves with no crust yet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: slaughtering the תודה before the loaves form a crust in the oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he slaughtered the תודה before the surface of the loaves formed a crust in the oven, the loaves do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes a new line. This sets up the next move, a search for the source of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, the loaves only become holy if they are already baked enough to have a crust when the תודה is slaughtered. The גמרא quotes this line now so that it can ask where the rule comes from.

phrases.english: He slaughtered it before
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. Its ruling is that in this case the loaves do not become holy.

phrases.english: its surface formed a crust in the oven.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרְמוּ פָּנֶיהָ בַּתַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the location argument to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loaves are not holy if the תודה was slaughtered before they formed a crust.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where these rules come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rules about when the loaves become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question covers more than the crust rule. It also covers the rule from the next משנה, that slaughtering שלא לשמה keeps the loaves from becoming holy. The answer will learn all of these from one פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches when the תודה loaves become holy

steps.title: The loaves need a crust
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'cakes of bread' that the loaves only become holy once they have a crust.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: "With cakes of leavened bread he shall bring his offering with the sacrifice." This teaches that the loaves are not holy unless their surface has formed a crust in the oven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about the תודה loaves. The first lesson is the crust rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls them "cakes of bread." Dough that has not yet formed a crust is not yet called bread. So the loaves must already have a crust to become holy.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "With cakes of leavened bread
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:13

phrases.english: he shall present his offering with the sacrifice" –
this teaches that the loaves are not holy

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קָרְמוּ פָּנֶיהָ בַּתַּנּוּר.
phrases.english: unless their surface formed a crust in the oven.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל חַלּוֹת לֶחֶם חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'cakes of bread' mean the loaves must already be bread, with a crust.

steps.title: The loaves become holy at the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The words 'he shall present his offering with the sacrifice' teach that the loaves become holy only when the תודה is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He shall present his offering with the sacrifice" teaches that the loaves become holy only through the slaughtering of the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns a second rule from the same פסוק: the moment the loaves become holy is the slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves are tied to the זבח, the sacrifice. So it is the slaughtering of that sacrifice that makes them holy. This explains why the משנה looks at what state the loaves are in at the time of slaughter.

phrases.english: "He shall present his offering with the sacrifice" –
this teaches that the loaves are not holy
except through the slaughtering of the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: יַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּנוֹ עַל זֶבַח מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵין הַלֶּחֶם קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁחִיטַת הַזֶּבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second lesson from the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves become holy at the moment the תודה is slaughtered.

steps.title: Slaughter for the wrong purpose does not make the loaves holy
steps.stepSummary: The words 'sacrifice of thanks' teach that if the תודה is slaughtered שלא לשמה, the loaves do not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The sacrifice of thanks" teaches that if he slaughtered it not for its own sake, the loaves do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns a third rule: the slaughter must be done as a תודה for the loaves to become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the loaves go with a "זבח תודה," a sacrifice of thanks. If it was slaughtered for a different purpose, it was not slaughtered as a תודה at that moment. So the loaves do not become holy. This is the source for the rule in the next משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrifice of thanks; the תודה offering
Not for their own sake; for a different purpose

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק teaches three rules: the loaves need a crust, they become holy at the slaughter, and a slaughter שלא לשמה does not make them holy.

phrases.english: "The sacrifice of thanks" –
this teaches that if he slaughtered not for their sake
the loaves did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶבַח תּוֹדַת מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאִם שָׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final lesson from the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves only become holy if the slaughter is done as a תודה.

steps.title: Half-baked מצה and pot-made מצה work for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one fulfills the מצוה of מצה with מצה נא and with מצה made in an אילפס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: one fulfills the obligation with half-baked מצה, and with מצה made in a stewpot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about eating מצה on פסח. It is related to the topic of how baked bread must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as we asked when the תודה loaves count as bread, this ברייתא says how baked מצה must be. It does not need to be fully baked, and it does not need to be baked in an oven. A pot is also fine.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One fulfills the obligation with half-done matza,
and with matza made in a stewpot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related topic: how baked bread must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half-baked מצה and מצה made in a pot both work for the מצוה.

steps.title: What counts as half-baked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מצה נא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is half-baked מצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term מצה נא from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מצה is too raw, it is not bread at all. So the גמרא needs to know exactly how baked it must be.

phrases.english: What is half-done matza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term in the ברייתא.

steps.title: שמואל's test: no threads of dough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל defines מצה נא as מצה that, when broken, has no threads of dough pulling out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is any מצה that, when you break it, no threads of dough stretch out from it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a simple test for when half-baked מצה is baked enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If threads of dough stretch out when you break the מצה, it is still raw dough. If no threads come out, it counts as bread, even though it is not fully baked.
steps.whatToRemember: מצה counts as baked once breaking it does not pull out threads of dough.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Any that, when one breaks it,
threads are not drawn out from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כֹּל שֶׁפּוֹרְסָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מצה נא is מצה that does not pull threads of dough when it is broken.

steps.title: רבא applies the half-baked bread rule to the loaves of a תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the same rule that applies to מצה נא also applies to the loaves of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And the same is true for the loaves of a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes שמואל's definition of half-baked bread from the last step and says it also counts for the loaves that come with a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said half-baked מצה that does not pull threads when broken is real bread for the מצוה of eating מצה. רבא adds that such loaves are also good enough to count as the bread of a תודה. So if the loaves were only this far along when the תודה was slaughtered, they still become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; the same rule applies
The loaves brought together with a thanks offering
With regard to; in the matter of

phrases.english: Rava said:
And so too with regard to the loaves of a thanks offering.
phrases.notes: "So too" points back to שמואל's half-baked bread that does not pull threads when broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends שמואל's definition of מצה נא to the loaves of a תודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half-baked loaves that do not pull threads when broken count as proper loaves for a תודה.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious, since both use the word 'bread'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: this is obvious, because the Torah uses the word לחם for both מצה and the loaves of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! Here it says 'bread,' and here it says 'bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רבא even needed to say this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls מצה 'bread' and also calls the loaves of a תודה 'bread.' If half-baked מצה already counts as bread, the same should clearly be true for the תודה loaves. So רבא's statement seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)
It is written in the פסוק

phrases.english: It is obvious!
Here, "bread" is written,
phrases.notes: About מצה: דברים 16:3.

phrases.english: and here, "bread" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's statement is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases use the same word, לחם, so the rule for מצה obviously carries over to the תודה. Saying it adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought half-baked bread counts as broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא was needed. Because the Torah says 'one' loaf, we might have treated half-baked bread like a broken piece, which is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: The Torah said 'one,' which means you may not take a broken piece, and this half-baked bread is like broken bread. So רבא teaches us that it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's statement is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תודה, the Torah says to take 'one' loaf from each kind. That teaches that the loaf must be whole, not a broken piece. Half-baked bread falls apart easily, so we might have treated it as already broken. רבא teaches that it still counts as one whole loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea the teaching corrects)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
A broken or sliced piece of bread
He teaches us (this is the new point)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
The Merciful One said "one"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14

phrases.english: to teach that one may not take a broken piece,
and this half-baked bread is like something already broken,
so he teaches us that it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reason the rule could have been different (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'one' requires a whole loaf, and half-baked bread that falls apart might count as broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: Half-baked loaves count as whole and are valid for the תודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Half-baked bread that does not pull threads counts as real, whole bread, both for מצה and for the loaves of a תודה.

steps.title: A תודה slaughtered with eighty loaves: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: A new argument: if someone slaughters a תודה with eighty loaves instead of forty, חזקיה says forty become holy and רבי יוחנן says none do.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: A תודה was slaughtered with eighty loaves. חזקיה says forty of the eighty become holy. רבי יוחנן says not even forty of the eighty become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, an argument between אמוראים about a תודה brought with double the required number of loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה needs exactly forty loaves. Here the person brought eighty. חזקיה says the extra loaves do not ruin things, so forty of them become holy. רבי יוחנן says the whole group fails, so no loaves become holy at all.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the loaves are 'too many to count.' He is saying that eighty loaves together never became holy, so not even forty of them did.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, תּוֹדָה שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ עַל שְׁמוֹנִים חַלּוֹת:
phrases.english: It was stated: a thanks offering that one slaughtered together with eighty loaves.
phrases.notes: A תודה normally comes with forty loaves.

phrases.aramaic: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים,
phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya says: Forty out of the eighty became holy.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Not even forty out of the eighty became holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, תּוֹדָה שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ עַל שְׁמוֹנִים חַלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about how the loaves become holy when the תודה is slaughtered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: forty of the eighty loaves become holy. רבי יוחנן: none of them become holy.

steps.title: רבי זירא: where both sides agree
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says both agree when the owner spelled out his intent. If he said 'let forty be holy,' they are. If he said 'only if all eighty are holy,' none are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Everyone agrees that if he said 'Let forty of the eighty become holy,' they become holy. If he said 'Forty should not become holy unless all eighty become holy,' they do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא narrows the argument by first showing two cases where חזקיה and רבי יוחנן agree. This sets up his explanation of where they really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner clearly said he wants only forty to be holy, everyone agrees forty become holy. If he clearly made it all eighty or nothing, everyone agrees none become holy, because eighty cannot be holy. So the argument cannot be about these clear cases.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he said

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Everyone agrees
that where he said:
"Let forty of the eighty become holy," they become holy;
and if he said: "Forty should not become holy

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִקְדְּשׁוּ שְׁמוֹנִים״ – לֹא קָדְשׁוּ.
phrases.english: unless eighty become holy," they do not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument from step 23 by showing where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner clearly intends forty, forty become holy. If he clearly requires all eighty, none become holy.

steps.title: The real argument: a backup, or one big offering?
steps.stepSummary: They argue only when the owner said nothing. חזקיה thinks the extra loaves were a backup. רבי יוחנן thinks he wanted one big offering of eighty.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue when he said nothing. One Sage thinks he meant the extra loaves as a backup. The other Sage thinks he meant to bring one large offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the true point of the argument: what a person most likely meant when he brought eighty loaves without saying anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה says the person really wanted forty and added more in case some got ruined, so forty become holy. רבי יוחנן says he wanted one big offering of eighty. Eighty can never be holy, so none of them are. The argument is about guessing the owner's intent, not about a law of the loaves themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A backup or guarantee, in case something is lost or ruined

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue only when the owner said nothing. חזקיה: the extra forty were a backup, so forty are holy. רבי יוחנן: he wanted one big offering, so none are holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the holiness of the loaves depends on what the owner intends. It turns a debate about loaves into a question about how we read a person's unspoken plan.

phrases.english: When do they argue? When he said nothing.
One Sage holds: He means the extra as a backup,
phrases.notes: This is חזקיה: extra loaves in case some get ruined.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לְקׇרְבָּן גָּדוֹל קָא מִיכַּוֵּין.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: He means to bring a large offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי זירא's explanation by naming the case they argue about and each side's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the owner said nothing, חזקיה assumes the extra loaves were a backup, so forty become holy. רבי יוחנן assumes he wanted a large offering, so none become holy.

steps.title: אביי: the argument is about vessels making things holy without intention
steps.stepSummary: אביי says both sides agree the extra forty loaves were a backup. They argue about whether כלי שרת make things holy even when the owner did not intend it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees the owner meant the extra loaves as a backup. They argue about whether holy vessels make things holy without the owner's intention. One side (חזקיה) says they do. The other side (רבי יוחנן) says they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different explanation of the argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן from Step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 25, the two sides disagreed about what the owner meant. אביי says they do not disagree about that, because both agree he meant the extra loaves as a backup. For אביי, the argument is about the power of כלי שרת: חזקיה says they make forty loaves holy even without the owner's intention, and רבי יוחנן says they need intention, so none become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: As a guarantee or backup, in case some loaves are ruined
Holy vessels used in the Temple service
Without intention, without the owner meaning it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up אביי with Step 25. There, the argument was about what the owner intended. For אביי, both sides agree about the owner's intention, and the argument is about what כלי שרת can do.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Everyone agrees that he intends them as a backup,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִכְלֵי שָׁרֵת מְקַדְּשִׁין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and they argue about whether service vessels make things holy without intention.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת מְקַדְּשִׁין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: service vessels make things holy without intention,
phrases.notes: The first 'Sage' is חזקיה, so forty loaves become holy. The second one is רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: service vessels do not make things holy without intention.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְאַחְרָיוּת קָא מִיכַּוֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רבי זירא's explanation in Step 25 for the argument in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree the extra loaves were a backup. חזקיה holds כלי שרת make things holy without intention, and רבי יוחנן holds they do not.

steps.title: רב פפא: the argument is about the knife
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says everyone agrees כלי שרת make things holy without intention. The argument is whether a סכין, which has no inside, makes things holy like other כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that holy vessels make things holy even without intention. Here they argue about the knife. One side (חזקיה) says the knife makes things holy like a holy vessel. The other side (רבי יוחנן) says that since a knife has no inside, it does not make things holy like a holy vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third explanation of the argument, and he moves the focus to the slaughtering knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא agrees with חזקיה's side in אביי's version, that כלי שרת work without intention. But he says the knife is a special case. A normal holy vessel holds things inside it, and a knife does not, so רבי יוחנן says it cannot make the loaves holy like a normal כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Knife (here, the knife used to slaughter the תודה)
An inside; a space that holds things

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת מְקַדְּשִׁין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that service vessels make things holy without intention,
and here they argue about the knife.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: סַכִּין מְקַדֶּשֶׁת כִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: a knife makes things holy like a service vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: סַכִּין, כֵּיוָן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ תּוֹךְ,
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: a knife, since it has no inside,
does not make things holy like a service vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת מְקַדְּשִׁין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts one side of אביי's question as agreed by everyone and moves the argument to the knife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees כלי שרת make things holy without intention. חזקיה holds the knife works like a כלי שרת. רבי יוחנן holds it does not, because it has no inside.

steps.title: A second version of רב פפא: is the knife stronger than other vessels?
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רב פפא: everyone agrees כלי שרת need intention. חזקיה says the סכין is stronger than other vessels, so it works even without intention. רבי יוחנן says it is not stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב פפא said this: Everyone agrees that holy vessels make things holy only with intention. Here they argue about the knife. One side (חזקיה) says the knife is stronger than a holy vessel, since it makes things holy even though it has no inside. The other side (רבי יוחנן) says the knife is not stronger than a holy vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב פפא's explanation that starts from the opposite rule about כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, everyone agrees that normal כלי שרת need intention. חזקיה reasons that a knife makes things holy even without an inside, which shows it is stronger than other vessels, so it also works without intention and forty loaves become holy. רבי יוחנן says the knife is no stronger, so like any כלי שרת it needs intention.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions of רב פפא start from opposite rules. In the first, everyone says כלי שרת work without intention. In the second, everyone says they need intention.
steps.whatToRemember: There are now four explanations of the argument: what the owner intended (רבי זירא), whether כלי שרת work without intention (אביי), whether a knife counts like a כלי שרת (רב פפא, first version), and whether a knife is stronger than a כלי שרת (רב פפא, second version).

phrases.english: And there are those who say that Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that service vessels make things holy only with intention,
and here they argue about the knife.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: סַכִּין אַלִּימָא מִכְּלִי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: a knife is stronger than a service vessel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לַיהּ תּוֹךְ – מְיקַדְּשָׁה,
phrases.english: since even though it has no inside, it makes things holy,
phrases.notes: Since the knife already does more than a normal vessel, חזקיה says it also works without intention.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: סַכִּין לָא אַלִּימָא (לַיהּ) מִכְּלִי שָׁרֵת.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: a knife is not stronger than a service vessel.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רב פפא's explanation from Step 27, starting from the opposite agreed rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees כלי שרת need intention. חזקיה holds the knife is stronger, so it works without intention. רבי יוחנן holds it is not stronger.

steps.title: משנה: wrong intention versus a טריפה animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if the תודה was slaughtered with a plan to eat it after its time or outside its place, the loaves still become holy. If the animal turns out to be a טריפה, the loaves do not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he slaughtered the תודה with the plan to eat it after its time or outside its place, the bread became holy. If he slaughtered it and it was found to be a טריפה, the bread did not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new משנה about which problems with the slaughter still allow the loaves to become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughter with a wrong intention about time (חוץ לזמנה) or place (חוץ למקומה) still makes the loaves holy, and they share the offering's problem. If the animal is found to be a טריפה, the loaves do not become holy at all. The טריפה defect was already there before the slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond its time: planning to eat or burn the offering after its allowed time
Outside its place: planning to eat or burn the offering outside its allowed area
An animal with a fatal defect, which cannot be used as an offering

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that not every problem with the animal stops the loaves from becoming holy. A wrong intention during the slaughter still makes the loaves holy, but a defect in the animal itself does not.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he slaughtered it beyond its time or outside its place,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the תודה. He means he slaughtered it while planning to eat it after its time or outside its area.

phrases.english: the bread became holy.
If he slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifa,
the bread did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁחָטָהּ חוּץ לִזְמַנָּהּ וְחוּץ לִמְקוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of the eighty loaves and opens a new משנה about when the loaves become holy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter with a wrong intention about time or place makes the loaves holy. Slaughter of an animal found to be a טריפה does not.

steps.title: A blemished animal: do the loaves become holy?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If the תודה was slaughtered and then found to have a מום, רבי אליעזר says the loaves became holy and the חכמים say they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered the תודה and it turned out to have a blemish, רבי אליעזר says the loaves became holy, and the חכמים say they did not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case to its list: the animal is slaughtered, and only afterward do we find out it has a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step we learned that a טריפה animal does not make the loaves holy. A מום is a different kind of problem, and here the משנה records a disagreement. רבי אליעזר says the loaves become holy, and the חכמים say they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a physical blemish, which is not fit to be brought as a קרבן

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it was found to be blemished,
Rabbi Eliezer says: it became holy,
and the Sages say: it did not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of cases from step 29 (חוץ לזמנו, חוץ למקומו, טריפה) with the case of a מום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה found to have a מום after slaughter: רבי אליעזר says the loaves become holy, and the חכמים say they do not.

steps.title: Slaughtered for the wrong purpose: the loaves do not become holy
steps.stepSummary: If the תודה, the איל המילואים, or the two כבשי עצרת were slaughtered שלא לשמה, the bread that comes with them does not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered the תודה for the sake of a different offering, the bread does not become holy. The same is true of the איל המילואים, and of the two sheep of שבועות that were slaughtered for a different purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a final case: the animal was slaughtered with the wrong purpose in mind. It applies the same rule to two other offerings that also came with bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is the purpose in the person's mind at the moment of slaughter, not a flaw in the animal's body. The משנה says that in this case the loaves do not become holy. It groups the תודה together with the איל המילואים and the כבשי עצרת, since all three are offerings whose slaughter makes bread holy.

keyTerms.meaning: not for its own sake, meaning slaughtered with the purpose of a different kind of offering
the inauguration ram brought when the משכן was set up, which came with loaves
the two sheep brought on שבועות together with the שתי הלחם
the bread that comes with the offering

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list ends here. A wrong plan about time or place (חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו) still lets the bread become holy. A טריפה does not, and neither does slaughter שלא לשמה. A מום is disputed.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it not for its sake,
phrases.notes: He slaughtered the תודה with a different offering in mind.

phrases.english: and likewise the ram of inauguration,
and likewise the two sheep of Atzeret
phrases.notes: עצרת here means שבועות.

phrases.english: that he slaughtered not for their sake –
the bread did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, וְכֵן אֵיל הַמִּילּוּאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list of cases with slaughter שלא לשמה, and extends the rule to two other offerings that come with bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the תודה, the איל המילואים, or the כבשי עצרת are slaughtered שלא לשמה, the bread does not become holy.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking whose opinion stands behind the משנה's rules. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave several rulings: some problems let the bread become holy and some do not. The גמרא wants to know which sage holds this exact set of rulings, so that we can understand the reasoning behind them.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is our משנה? (the question of which תנא it follows)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishna, whose is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה into the גמרא and asks who authored its rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the משנה's rulings about when the bread becomes holy.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר: the rule of before and after the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי מאיר. A ברייתא gives the general rule: if the problem came before the slaughter, the bread does not become holy; if it came after, the bread does become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר. As a ברייתא teaches: This is the rule. Any case where the problem came before the slaughter, the bread does not become holy. If the problem came after the slaughter, the bread becomes holy. If he slaughtered it with a plan to eat it after its time or outside its place, the bread becomes holy. If he slaughtered it and it turned out to be a טריפה, the bread does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. It quotes a ברייתא that lays out one clear rule that explains the משנה's cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is when the problem started. A טריפה was already damaged before it was slaughtered, so the bread never becomes holy. A wrong plan about time or place is formed only during the slaughter itself, so the animal was fine up to the slaughter and the bread does become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: its disqualification, meaning the problem that makes the offering unfit
a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's test is simple: did the problem exist before the slaughter (then the bread does not become holy), or did it come only with or after the slaughter (then the bread becomes holy)? That is how the משנה can treat חוץ לזמנו and טריפה so differently.
steps.confusionAlert: A plan to eat the offering after its time is made during the slaughter, yet the ברייתא counts it as a problem that comes "after." What matters is that the animal itself was fine until the slaughter, unlike a טריפה, which was damaged before it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This before-and-after rule is the tool for deciding any case of a flawed תודה, and it gives the reasoning behind the whole משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir.
As it is taught: This is the rule:
Any case whose disqualification is before the slaughter –
the bread did not become holy;
if its disqualification is after the slaughter –
the bread became holy.
If he slaughtered it outside its time or outside its place –
phrases.notes: He slaughtered it while planning to eat it after its time, or outside its proper place.

phrases.english: the bread became holy;
if he slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifa –
the bread did not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32 and supports the answer with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, whose rule is quoted in the ברייתא: a problem before the slaughter means the bread does not become holy, and a problem after it means the bread does become holy.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה matches a known opinion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that begins זֶה הַכְּלָל, which gives the same rulings for חוץ לזמנו, חוץ למקומו, and טריפה.
